ISS-016.title: chat streaming route drops first generated token via bogus prompt-prefix strip

DEC-037.title: ISS-153 reserved-special-token semantics is intended; no literal-<PAD> escape added
DEC-037.rationale: SimpleCharacterTokenizer reserves the multi-char markers <PAD>/<EOS>/<BOS>: encode('<PAD>') returns the single pad id, matching every mainstream tokenizer (HF <pad> binding, BPE specials). This is the SAME property ISS-152 deliberately relies on (encode('<EOS>') must be one token so eval generations stop on the model's EOS). Reachability of the alleged corruption is near-zero: TextDataset/SFT/DPO encode whole files/samples at once, so <PAD> embedded in real content is preserved char-by-char; only a standalone 5-char sample that is EXACTLY '<PAD>' collapses. The decode-sided ambiguity ([pad_id] and the char sequence both decode to '<PAD>') is inherent to appending a multi-char reserved token whose constituents may also be in the corpus. Making markers literal-expressible would break encode('<EOS>')==[eos_id] (ISS-152) and round-tripping; the fix would be a behavior regression for no real-world gain.
DEC-037.alternatives_rejected: (1) encode specials as literal char sequences when the chars are in the corpus -- reverts ISS-152's single-token EOS encode and breaks eval stopping; (2) add an escape syntax (e.g. '\<PAD>\') -- scope creep, no consumer needs it, and every tokenizer that reserves specials has the same limitation; (3) leave as-is -- matches the industry-standard reserved-token contract and the deliberate ISS-152 behavior, impact localized to an unreachable pathological input.

EV-167.source: round61 live runs: encode('rec <PAD> ord') expands char-by-char (collision unreachable in text-file datasets); encode('<PAD>')==[pad_id] is the HF-style reserved binding; decode([pad])==decode([<,P,A,D,>])==='<PAD>'
